36-091.r: Aspartame → artificial sweetener; Freon → refrigerant; neoprene → synthetic rubber; Benadryl → anti-histamine.

36-092.r: All correct: lipstick → lead (common impurity); soft drinks → brominated vegetable oil (emulsifier in citrus drinks); Chinese fast food → monosodium glutamate (MSG).

36-093.r: Potassium bromide → photography; potassium nitrate → gunpowder; potassium sulphate → fertilizer; monopotassium tartrate → bakery.

36-094.r: Correct pair: ozone depletion → skin cancer. Fixes: sulfur dioxide → acid rain; fluoride pollution → teeth; methyl isocyanate → Bhopal gas tragedy.

36-095.r: Phenyl (emulsion of light creosote oil, water, soap) → household germicide because it is a phenol derivative and phenol is a germicide → A and R true, R explains A.

36-096.r: Rutherford → atom bomb; Alfred Nobel → dynamite; Cartwright → powerloom; Graham Bell → telephone.

36-097.r: Technology Day → 11 May (Pokhran test 1998); Photography Day → 19 August; National Sports Day → 29 August (Dhyan Chand's birthday); Nagasaki Day → 9 August.

36-098.r: UN year 2011 → International Year of Chemistry (and of Forests). 2023 → Millets; 2024 → Camelids; 2025 → Quantum Science and Technology, Cooperatives, Glaciers' Preservation.

36-099.r: UN year 2025 → International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, marking 100 years of quantum mechanics.

36-100.r: UNFCCC → mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, CO2 included → 'more than one'. Paris Climate Change Agreement signed 22 April 2016 by 175 countries/organisations, including India.

36-101.r: Correct: Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) → primary healthcare; Talanoa Dialogue → climate change. Wrong: Hague Convention (1980) → child abduction; Under2 Coalition → climate action → 1 and 3.
36-101.t: Under2 Coalition is about climate, not child rights; Hague Convention here is about child abduction.

36-102.r: Mandatory ethanol blending with gasoline → Brazil (since 1976); since 2007 the legal blend is about 25% ethanol, 75% gasoline.

36-103.r: Inorganic gaseous air pollutants → hydrogen cyanide and hydrogen sulphide (book accepts both); others: CO2, CO, SO2, nitrous oxide, nitrogen dioxide.

36-104.r: Chief source of hydrogen sulphide (H2S, rotten-egg smell) → decaying vegetation and animal matter; also bacterial breakdown of wastes, sewage plants, landfills, geothermal fields.

36-105.r: Carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide and methane → all greenhouse gases causing global warming → 'more than one'.

36-106.r: Contribution to global warming → CO2 (about 26%) > methane (4-9%) > nitrous oxide (about 1.5%) > CFCs (0.1-0.4%); water vapour about 60%.

36-107.r: India's CO2: about 2 t per capita (1.922 t in 2023), not under 0.5 t; second in Asia-Pacific after China; electricity and heat producers largest source → II, III.

36-108.r: Water vapour → decreases with altitude (true); NOT maximum at poles: highest in warm wet tropics, less than one percent in deserts and polar regions → 1 only.

36-109.r: Wet-bulb temperature (air temperature + humidity) of 35°C → upper limit for human life: sweat cannot evaporate to cool the body → only statement II.

36-110.r: Nuclear (and thermal) power plants → thermal pollution: heated coolant water returned to nature cuts oxygen supply and harms ecosystems.

36-111.r: Green muffler → against noise pollution: 4-5 rows of dense trees planted along roads, industrial areas and other noisy places.

36-112.r: Magnetic (magnetite) particles linked to neurodegenerative problems → come from vehicle brakes, vehicle engines and power plants → 1, 2, 4.

36-113.r: Incomplete burning of petrol and diesel (poor air supply) → carbon monoxide (poisonous) and soot instead of carbon dioxide.

36-114.r: The book gives no single answer (*): city smoke holds CO, CO2, nitrogen oxides, SO2, lead and ozone, so every option fits; the commission did not evaluate it.

36-115.r: Particulate matter (PM, particle pollution) → air pollutant: tiny particles and liquid droplets that harm the heart and lungs when inhaled.

36-116.r: RSPM (Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter) → the fraction of suspended particles readily inhaled; among options, size less than 5 µm.

36-117.r: NAMP (run by CPCB) → SO2, NO2, suspended particulate matter and fine particulate matter monitored at all locations; network 966 stations in 419 cities (November 2024).

36-118.r: Steam methane reforming (methane + steam, 700–1000°C, nickel catalyst) → grey hydrogen if CO2 is released; blue if CO2 is captured. Green → renewable energy; brown → coal.
36-118.h: Colour code: Grey = gas, CO2 out; Blue = gas, CO2 stored; Green = renewable; Brown = coal.

36-119.r: Green hydrogen (made with renewable energy) → can replace fossil feedstocks in fertilizer production, petroleum refining and steel making → all three.

36-120.r: Green hydrogen → direct fuel for internal combustion, blended with natural gas for heat or power, and in fuel cells to run vehicles → all three correct.

36-121.r: Smog (smoke + fog) → mainly oxides of nitrogen and sulfur, with ozone, smoke and particulates; from coal, vehicles, industry and fires.

36-122.r: Photochemical smog (solar UV acting on hydrocarbons + nitrogen oxides) → always contains ozone, its principal component; a brownish-grey haze.

36-123.r: Eutrophication → nutrient enrichment of a water body; algae grow heavily and dissolved oxygen gets depleted → both correct.

36-124.r: Eutrophication results from → high amounts of nitrogenous nutrients (nitrate) and orthophosphates (also silicate); natural, but made worse by humans.
36-124.t: Algal bloom and oxygen depletion are effects; nutrient overload is the cause.

36-125.r: BOD (Biological Oxygen Demand) → standard measure of pollution in aquatic ecosystems: oxygen used by microbes decomposing organic matter; higher BOD = more polluted water.

36-126.r: Physico-chemical changes in water sources → effluents (outflow from sewage treatment or industrial wastewater).

36-127.r: Membrane bioreactors (MBR) → wastewater treatment: membrane separation combined with conventional treatment, used in municipal and industrial plants.

36-128.r: Activated carbon removes pollutants from effluents: large surface area adsorbs heavy metals, and it is easily made from carbon-rich wastes → II and III true, both explain I.

36-129.r: Pyrolysis and plasma gasification → waste-to-energy technologies: high-temperature breakdown of waste using nil or little oxygen.

36-130.r: Mercury pollution sources → all four: pesticides, dental amalgam fillings, fluorescent lamps, coal-based thermal power plants.

37-001.r: Zoology → study of both living and extinct (dead) animals: structure, embryology, evolution, classification; Aristotle = Father of Zoology.

37-002.r: Birds → ornithology; inheritance → genetics; environment → ecology; fossils → palaeobiology.

37-003.r: Study of flowers → anthology. Phrenology → human skull; agrostology → grasses; palynology → pollen grains and spores.

37-004.r: Insects → entomology. Ichthyology → fish; parasitology → parasites; malacology → molluscs and shells.

37-005.r: Demography → statistical study of populations, including humans. Ecology → organisms and environment; genetics → heredity and variation; virology → viruses.

37-006.r: Ethnology → comparative study of cultures (races of mankind). Ethnography → a specific culture; ethology → animal behaviour; ethics → moral duties.

37-007.r: Bionics → studying biological systems in nature and using that knowledge in machines. Bionomics → organism and environment; biometry → statistics in biology.

37-008.r: Palaeobotany → plant fossils (plant remains from geological contexts), so 'none of these'; Birbal Sahni = Father of Indian Palaeobotany.
37-008.t: Palaeobotany is plant fossils, not animal fossils.

37-009.r: Rearing silkworms → sericulture. Apiculture → bees; horticulture → fruit and flower plants; floriculture → flowers.

37-011.r: Wrong pair: vegetable cultivation – horticulture → specific term is olericulture (a branch of horticulture). Correct: floriculture – flowers; agronomy – crops; pomology – fruits.

37-012.r: Growing vegetables → olericulture (culture of non-woody plants for food).
37-012.t: Pomology → fruits; floriculture → flowers; olericulture → vegetables.

37-013.r: Wrong pair: pisciculture – lac insect → pisciculture is fish rearing (fish hatchery). Correct: apiculture – honey bee; sericulture – silkworm; horticulture – flower.
